My logic was to test player 9's behavior because the consensus was already leaning heavily toward player 7, and I wanted to see if anyone else would break from the pack. It was a risky strategy, but it shows I was analyzing individual behavior rather than just following the crowd.

Player 8, you keep describing your Day 3 vote against me as a 'calculated risk' or a 'process', but you haven't explained why you deemed a random player more suspicious than a known wolf. In a game where every vote counts to remove threats, choosing to split the village vote is objectively anti-village. Everyone else recognized player 7 was the priority; your attempt to reframe your inaction or distraction as 'scrutiny' is exactly the kind of behavior that protects a wolf or serial killer.
